bugs.error_message: AccessKeyControllerTest/AuthControllerTest: all requests return 200 with empty body, isForbidden() assertions fail with 'Status expected:<403> but was:<200>'
bugs.root_cause: @MockBean SessionCookieAuthFilter (a concrete OncePerRequestFilter wired into the Spring Security chain via SecurityConfig.addFilterBefore) causes Mockito to mock doFilter() itself to a no-op that never calls chain.doFilter() — every request is silently swallowed by the mocked filter, so the controller is never invoked and MockMvc sees a default empty 200 response. Separately, LocalProfileAuthFilter (@Profile("!prod")) is also auto-included by @WebMvcTest since no profile is active by default in tests, so it auto-grants SUPERUSER to every request, defeating the withoutSuperuserRole_isForbidden tests too.
bugs.fix: Never @MockBean a Filter bean that's part of the security chain. Instead mock its real constructor dependencies (UserSessionRepository, AccessKeyRepository) so the real filter runs, and add @ActiveProfiles("prod") to the @WebMvcTest so LocalProfileAuthFilter (@Profile("!prod")) is excluded, matching real prod auth behavior.

POST /api/auth/keys/{id}/revoke -> 500 InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException: No EntityManager with actual transaction available for current thread - cannot reliably process 'remove' call
bugs.root_cause: AccessKeyService.revoke() called userSessionRepository.deleteByAccessKeyId(id), a Spring Data JPA derived delete query. Unlike save()/findById(), a derived deleteBy... query loads-then-removes each entity via entityManager.remove(), which requires an actual writable transaction bound to the thread -- the repository proxy does not provide one for this call path on its own. Only found by manually exercising the endpoint end-to-end via curl against the running dev backend; the Mockito-based AccessKeyServiceTest mocks the repository entirely, so it never touches a real EntityManager/transaction and couldn't catch this.
bugs.fix: Added @Transactional to AccessKeyService.revoke(), matching the project's existing convention (WhListingService, WhItemService, etc. annotate service methods that perform repository writes/deletes beyond a single save()).

bugs.error_message: No qualifying bean of type 'org.springdoc.core.providers.ObjectMapperProvider' available: expected at least 1 bean which qualifies as autowire candidate. Dependency annotations: {}
bugs.root_cause: polymorphicModelConverter bean unconditionally required ObjectMapperProvider, which springdoc only autoconfigures when its own api-docs/swagger-ui are enabled. application-prod.yml sets springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false, so this crashed context startup whenever the prod profile actually ran (never caught before since dev never disables springdoc, and prod profile was never manually tested locally until the P2 auth-testing session).
bugs.fix: Added @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "springdoc.api-docs.enabled", havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = true) to the polymorphicModelConverter bean method.

Frontend spammed POST /api/listings/{id}/lookup in an infinite loop, every request returning 403, observed while manually testing the prod auth profile as GUEST
bugs.root_cause: item-research.ts:92-107 has an effect that auto-triggers ExtractionStore.lookup() whenever !lookupResults[id] && !lookupLoadingIds.includes(id). The old error handler in ExtractionStore.lookup() only cleared lookupLoadingIds on failure, never set lookupResults — so the effect's guard condition became true again immediately after every failed request, re-firing forever. Never surfaced before because dev always runs as SUPERUSER (LocalProfileAuthFilter), so lookup calls never got a 403 — first GUEST-as-prod-profile test exposed it. Same class of gap already flagged in berechtigungen-konzept.md Kap. 8 ("AI-UI-Elemente nicht statusabhängig ausblenden"), but this is worse than a hidden-button UX gap: it's a real self-inflicted request-flood against the own backend.
bugs.fix: lookup()'s error handler now also patches lookupResults[whItemId] to a minimal { lookupStatus: 'ERROR', ... } result (status already existed in LookupResult model and is already rendered by item-research.html:125), so the effect's guard condition goes false and the loop stops after the first failed attempt.

bugs.error_message: Backend log showed scheduleExtraction (DL-Extraktion, LLM call) running for a GUEST session, discovered during manual auth testing — user asked "unklar ist mir auch, warum überhaupt eine Suche durchgeführt wurde"
bugs.root_cause: openDetail() unconditionally scheduled dlOrchestrationService.scheduleExtraction(itemText) in its afterCommit hook on every detail view. The detail endpoint itself is public (normale Suche, Konzept Kap. 1), so GUEST users silently triggered LLM/provider-quota-consuming AI calls just by opening a listing — completely bypassing the auth model, which was built specifically to gate AI access behind a session.
bugs.fix: Read SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication() before the afterCommit hook; only call scheduleExtraction() when an authenticated principal is present (USER/SUPERUSER). Detail view itself stays public and unaffected.

bugs.error_message: User found the Zugriffscode input in Settings fully editable/enabled while running as Local-Dev-Superuser (no key), expected a locked field with an explanatory subtitle instead
bugs.root_cause: LocalProfileAuthFilter is registered before SessionCookieAuthFilter (SecurityConfig.filterChain) and unconditionally sets the SUPERUSER principal whenever no Authentication exists yet — so SessionCookieAuthFilter's cookie check (guarded by "if authentication == null") never runs while the !prod profile is active. Logging in with a real access key while running plain dev therefore creates a session row and cookie that are silently never read back — a functional no-op the UI didn't disclose.
bugs.fix: Added SettingsComponent.isLocalSuperuser computed (auth.isSuperuser() && !auth.hasKey() — distinguishes Local-dev-auto-superuser from a real GUEST). Settings now shows a disabled field+button with an italic hint explaining the login has no effect here, instead of a misleadingly functional form.

bugs.error_message: User noticed hundreds of "[GoogleDiscovery] Skipping locale duplicate" TRACE lines for a single printer product lookup
bugs.root_cause: canonicalizePath() built the dedup key from host+path only, dropping the query string entirely. For domains like druckerchannel.de, distinct pages are addressed purely via query params (techinfo.php?m[]=1477 vs techinfo.php?m[]=6264, device_info.php?ID=4899 vs ?ID=4900) — all of these collapsed onto the same canonical key (e.g. "druckerchannel.de/techinfo.php") and got wrongly discarded as duplicates by the HashSet check in mapSdkResults(). The locale-prefix-stripping the method was meant for (/de/ vs /us/ same-content variants) never needed query stripping — that was an unintended side effect of using uri.getPath() instead of the full path+query.
bugs.fix: canonicalizePath() now appends the query string back onto the canonicalized path (still strips only the locale path prefix). Distinct query-addressed pages are no longer falsely deduped, so the loop needs far fewer Google Discovery result pages to fill resultCount and returns the actually-different pages it was dropping before.

bugs.error_message: GUEST (confirmed via header showing 'Gast') still triggered scheduleExtraction on opening a listing detail — the bug-081 fix (SecurityContextHolder-based GUEST gating in WhItemService.openDetail()) did not actually prevent it, found via manual re-test
bugs.root_cause: The bug-081 fix checked `authentication != null && authentication.isAuthenticated()`, but SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication() is NEVER null by the time a request reaches the Service layer — Spring Security's built-in AnonymousAuthenticationFilter (runs after our custom SessionCookieAuthFilter, confirmed via the whitelabel-error-page stack trace) fills the gap with a non-null AnonymousAuthenticationToken that already has isAuthenticated()==true for true GUEST requests. So the guard was always true regardless of real auth state.
bugs.fix: Changed the check to `authentication.getPrincipal() instanceof QuerCheckerPrincipal` — only our own custom filters (LocalProfileAuthFilter/SessionCookieAuthFilter) ever set that principal type; Spring's anonymous fallback uses a plain String ("anonymousUser") principal, so it correctly evaluates to false for real GUEST. Mirrors the same check AuthService.me() already used correctly.
